He attended [[Bowie High School (Arlington, Texas)|Bowie High School]] in his hometown of [[Arlington, Texas]], before transferring to [[Montverde Academy]] in Florida, where he was rated a consensus five-star [[College recruiting|recruit]] and among the top players in the 2020 class by major recruiting services. As a senior, he led one of the best high school teams in history and received [[List of U.S. high school basketball national player of the year awards|national player of the year]] recognition. Cunningham committed to playing [[college basketball]] for the [[Oklahoma State Cowboys basketball|Oklahoma State Cowboys]], and was named a consensus first-team [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]] and [[Big 12 Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Big 12 Player of the Year]] after his freshman season with the team. He won a gold medal with the [[United States men's national under-19 basketball team|United States]] at the [[2019 FIBA Under-19 Basketball World Cup|2019 FIBA Under-19 World Cup]]. He was the [[NBA first overall]] pick by the Detroit Pistons in the [[2021 NBA draft]]. He was named as an [[List of NBA All-Stars|NBA All-Star]] and to an [[All-NBA Team]] for the first time in 2025. ==Early life and career== Cunningham was born in [[Arlington, Texas]], to Carrie and Keith Cunningham.{{cite web |title=Cade Cunningham |url=https://www.usab.com/basketball/players/mens/c/cunningham-cade.aspx |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190702195615/https://www.usab.com/basketball/players/mens/c/cunningham-cade.aspx |url-status=dead |archive-date=July 2, 2019 |publisher=[[USA Basketball]] |access-date=July 1, 2019 |date=June 20, 2019}} He grew up playing [[American football|football]] as a [[quarterback]], which he believes helped him become a better passer and leader on the basketball court. He focused on basketball after watching his brother play the sport in college.{{cite web |last=Francisco |first=Alexandra |title=Quarterback of the court: How football helped Cade Cunningham become a 5-star basketball prospect |url=https://www.masslive.com/hoophallclassic/2019/01/cade_cunningham.html |website=[[The Republican (Springfield, Massachusetts)|The Republican]] |access-date=July 1, 2019 |date=January 21, 2019}} He frequently played basketball with his father and brother at a [[recreation#Recreation center|recreation center]].{{cite web |last=Daniels |first=Evan |title=Cade Cunningham excels with u19 team, talks recruiting |url=https://247sports.com/college/basketball/recruiting/Article/Cade-Cunningham-FIBA-u19-Oklahoma-State-North-Carolina-Duke-133331030/ |publisher=[[247Sports.com|247Sports]] |access-date=July 1, 2019 |date=July 1, 2019}} He played the [[point guard]] position for Barnett Junior High School in Arlington.{{cite web |last=Wright |first=Mark |title=Towering Bowie freshman plays like a standout at age 15 |url=https://www.star-telegram.com/news/local/community/arlington-citizen-journal/article129305124.html |website=[[Fort Worth Star-Telegram]] |access-date=July 1, 2019 |date=January 27, 2017}} Since his childhood, he competed for the Texas Titans on the [[Amateur Athletic Union]] circuit alongside future [[TCU Horned Frogs men's basketball|TCU]] player [[Mike Miles Jr.]]{{cite web |last=Unruh |first=Jacob |title=OSU basketball: Cade Cunningham faces unique challenge this week — his close friends |url=https://www.oklahoman.com/story/sports/columns/2020/12/16/osu-basketball-cade-cunningham-faces-unique-challenge-this-week-his-close-friends/316893007/ |website=[[The Oklahoman]] |access-date=July 16, 2021 |date=December 15, 2020}} ==High school career== Cade Cunningham attended [[Bowie High School (Arlington, Texas)|Bowie High School]] in Arlington. He became a starter on the [[varsity team]] early in his freshman season. The team also featured [[Kyler Edwards]].{{cite web |last=Scitt |first=Marshall |title=Cade Arrives: How an Unlikely No. 1 Recruit Starts a New Era for OSU Hoops |url=https://pistolsfiringblog.com/cade-arrives-how-an-unlikely-no-1-recruit-starts-a-new-era-for-osu-hoops/ |website=Pistols Firing |access-date=July 16, 2021 |date=November 25, 2020}} Cunningham averaged 15.2 points, 6.4 rebounds, and 3.0 assists per game, helping Bowie reach the District 6A Region I final. He was subsequently named District 4-6A Newcomer of the Year.{{cite web |last=Gosset |first=Brian |title=One of the top basketball prospects in DFW is moving out of state to a national power |url=https://www.star-telegram.com/sports/dfwvarsity/boys-prep-basketball/article215176365.html |url-status=live|website=[[Fort Worth Star-Telegram]] |access-date=July 2, 2019 |date=July 19, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190702195614/https://www.star-telegram.com/sports/dfwvarsity/boys-prep-basketball/article215176365.html|archive-date=July 2, 2019}} In December 2017, early in his sophomore season, he suffered an injury while attempting to [[Slam dunk|dunk]] at a tournament in [[Houston]].{{cite web |last=Wright |first=Mark |title=Why this team isn't freaking out about an injury to its standout sophomore |url=https://www.star-telegram.com/sports/dfwvarsity/boys-prep-basketball/article190016934.html |website=[[Fort Worth Star-Telegram]] |access-date=July 1, 2019 |date=December 15, 2017}} Cunningham finished the season averaging 18.8 points, 8.2 rebounds, and 5.3 assists per game. He was named District 4-6A co-[[most valuable player]] (MVP) and earned Texas Association of Basketball Coaches All-Region honors.{{cite web |title=2018 SportsDayHS boys basketball All-District lists for area teams |url=https://sportsday.dallasnews.com/high-school/high-schools/2018/03/22/2018-sportsdayhs-boys-basketball-district-lists-area-teams |website=[[The Dallas Morning News]] |access-date=July 2, 2019 |date=March 22, 2018}} [[File:Cade Cunningham.jpg|thumb|left|upright|Cunningham with the Texas Titans at the [[EYBL]] in 2019]] Entering his junior year, Cunningham transferred to [[Montverde Academy]], a school in [[Montverde, Florida]] with a successful basketball program. He chose Montverde, whose team was ranked number one in the country by ''[[USA Today]]'', for its academics and coaching.{{cite web |last=Riddle |first=Greg |title=Why 5-star basketball recruit Cade Cunningham is leaving Arlington Bowie to join the nation's No. 1 HS team |url=https://sportsday.dallasnews.com/high-school/high-schools/2018/07/20/see-five-star-basketball-recruit-cade-cunningham-leaving-arlington-bowie-join-no-1-high-school-team-nation |website=[[The Dallas Morning News]] |access-date=July 2, 2019 |date=July 20, 2018}} On February 2, 2019, at the National Hoopfest tournament, Cunningham recorded 26 points, nine assists, and seven rebounds in a 76–51 win against [[Oak Hill Academy (Mouth of Wilson, Virginia)|Oak Hill Academy]], one of the top high school teams nationally.{{cite web |last=Collings |first=Buddy |title=Montverde beats Oak Hill at Hoopfest in Tampa |url=https://www.orlandosentinel.com/sports/highschool/os-sp-hs-bkb-hoopfest-0202-story.html |website=[[Orlando Sentinel]] |access-date=July 2, 2019 |date=February 2, 2019}} By the end of his junior season, he was averaging 11.4 points, 5.7 rebounds, and 5.5 assists per game.{{cite web |last=Divens |first=Jordan |title=2018-19 MaxPreps Boys Basketball Junior All-American Team |url=https://www.maxpreps.com/news/Unx8d7lBbEmJkCDKNtEhCw/2018-19-maxpreps-boys-basketball-junior-all-american-team.htm |publisher=[[MaxPreps]] |access-date=July 2, 2019 |date=April 17, 2019}} Following the high school season, Cunningham was named [[Nike Elite Youth Basketball League]] (EYBL) MVP after averaging 25.1 points, 6.6 rebounds, and 5.2 assists per game for the Texas Titans in the EYBL regular season.{{cite web |title=Nike EYBL Most Valuable Player: Cade Cunningham |url=https://www.d1circuit.com/news_article/show/1031816 |publisher=D1 Circuit |access-date=August 11, 2019 |date=July 5, 2019}} He was teammates with [[Greg Brown III|Greg Brown]] and [[Mike Miles Jr.]] with the Titans.{{cite web |last=Cook |first=Lyndon |title=Cunningham continues the Texas Titans - Drive Nation summer arms race |url=https://texashoops.rivals.com/news/cunningham-continues-the-texas-titans-drive-nation-summer-arms-race |website=[[Rivals.com|Rivals]] |access-date=July 16, 2021 |date=January 8, 2019}} For his senior season at Montverde, he was joined by many more top recruits, including five-star forwards [[Scottie Barnes]] and [[Day'Ron Sharpe]]. Many analysts regarded his team as one of the best in high school basketball history.{{cite web |last=O'Donnell |first=Ricky |title=Why Montverde is being called the best high school basketball team ever |url=https://www.sbnation.com/college-basketball/2020/1/21/21073999/montverde-basketball-roster-cade-cunningham-scottie-barnes-nba-talent-caleb-houstan |publisher=[[SB Nation]] |access-date=January 23, 2020 |date=January 21, 2020}} Cunningham averaged 13.9 points, 6.4 assists and 4.2 rebounds per game, leading Montverde to a 25–0 record with an average margin of victory of 39 points. He played only 22 minutes per game due to the depth of his team.{{cite web |last=Divens |first=Jordan |title=MaxPreps 2019-20 High School Boys Basketball Player of the Year: Cade Cunningham |url=https://www.maxpreps.com/news/Pe--2iLJfkuLqD7ecx_MOA/maxpreps-2019-20-high-school-boys-basketball-player-of-the-year--cade-cunningham.htm |publisher=[[MaxPreps]] |access-date=March 30, 2020 |date=March 25, 2020}} At the end of the season, Cunningham was honored as [[Mr. Basketball USA]], [[Naismith Prep Player of the Year Award|Naismith Prep Player of the Year]], and [[MaxPreps National Basketball Player of the Year awards|MaxPreps National Player of the Year]].{{cite web |last=Nagel |first=Cody |title=Cade Cunningham earns Naismith Player of the Year honor |url=https://247sports.com/college/oklahoma-state/Article/Oklahoma-State-Cowboys-basketball-recruiting-Cade-Cunningham-earns-Naismith-Player-of-the-Year-144879616/ |publisher=[[247Sports.com|247Sports]] |access-date=March 12, 2020 |date=March 11, 2020}} He was selected to play in the [[2020 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|McDonald's All-American Game]], [[Jordan Brand Classic]], and [[Nike Hoop Summit]], but all three games were canceled due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic]].{{cite magazine |last=Jordan |first=Jason |title=McDonald's All American Game Cancelled Amid COVID-19 Concerns |url=https://www.si.com/college/recruiting/basketball/mcdonalds-all-american-covid19-coronavirus-ncaa-tournament |magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]] |access-date=March 30, 2020 |date=March 12, 2019}} ===Recruiting=== Cunningham emerged as a top-25 recruit in the 2020 class at the end of his sophomore season at Bowie. He was a consensus five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and one of the best players in his class.{{cite web |last=O'Donnell |first=Ricky |title=Cade Cunningham is made for modern basketball |url=https://www.sbnation.com/college-basketball/2019/7/26/8906439/cade-cunningham-recruiting-nba-draft-scouting-report-montverde-high-school |publisher=[[SB Nation]] |access-date=August 11, 2019 |date=July 26, 2019}} Cunningham received offers from top [[NCAA Division I]] programs including [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke]], [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]], and [[North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball|North Carolina]], but many analysts viewed [[Oklahoma State Cowboys basketball|Oklahoma State]] as his likely destination after the program hired his brother {{ill|Cannen Cunningham|pl|lt=Cannen}} as an assistant coach.{{cite web |title=Cade Cunningham, Montverde Academy, Combo Guard |url=https://247sports.com/Player/Cade-Cunningham-46047476/ |publisher=[[247Sports.com]] |access-date=August 12, 2019}} On November 5, 2019, Cade Cunningham announced his commitment to Oklahoma State. He became the highest-ranked committed recruit in program history and the first five-star recruit to join Oklahoma State since [[Marcus Smart]] in 2012.{{cite web |title=Cade Cunningham commits to Oklahoma State |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/cade-cunningham-commits-oklahoma-state-235824347.html |publisher=[[Yahoo Sports]] |date=November 5, 2019 |access-date=November 5, 2019}} In June 2020, the NCAA imposed a postseason ban on Oklahoma State. Cunningham announced on June 22 that he would still play for the team.{{cite news |last=Borzello |first=Jeff |title=Top recruit Cade Cunningham still going to Oklahoma State despite postseason ban |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/29347312 |access-date=June 22, 2020 |work=[[ESPN]] |date=June 22, 2020}} {{College Athlete Recruit Start|40=no|collapse=no|year=2020}} |url=https://okstate.com/news/2020/11/25/mens-basketball-cunningham-double-double-helps-oklahoma-st-top-ut-arlington.aspx |website=[[Oklahoma State Cowboys]] |access-date=November 26, 2020 |title=Cunningham outduels Abmas, Oklahoma St. beats Oral Roberts |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401261732 |website=[[ESPN]] |publisher=[[Associated Press]] basketball|Wichita State]] 67–64.{{cite web |last=Boone |first=Kyle |title=Watch: Oklahoma State star freshman Cade Cunningham buries late game-winning shot to beat Wichita State |url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/watch-oklahoma-state-star-freshman-cade-cunningham-buries-late-game-winning-shot-to-beat-wichita-state/ |website=CBS Sports |access-date=January 26, 2021 |date=December 12, 2020}} On February 27, 2021, he posted a career-high 40 points and 11 rebounds in a 94–90 overtime win against [[Oklahoma Sooners men's basketball|Oklahoma]].{{cite web |last=Medcalf |first=Myron |title=Cade Cunningham powers Oklahoma State's NCAA tournament bid -- but will the Cowboys be allowed in? |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/30975498 |website=[[ESPN]] |access-date=February 28, 2021 |date=February 27, 2021}} The performance helped him earn Oscar Robertson National Player of the Week honors.{{cite web |title=Oklahoma State's Cunningham is Oscar Robertson National Player of the Week |url=http://www.sportswriters.net/usbwa/news/2021/oscar210302.html |publisher=[[United States Basketball Writers Association]] |access-date=July 16, 2021 |date=March 2, 2021}} Cunningham posted 25 points, eight rebounds, and five assists in an 83–74 upset win against top-seeded [[Baylor Bears men's basketball|Baylor]] in the [[2021 Big 12 men's basketball tournament|Big 12 tournament]] semifinals on March 12, 2021.{{cite web |last=Borzello |first=Jeff |title=Oklahoma State stuns Baylor, nears 'vision' of Big 12 men's tournament title |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/31054479 |website=[[ESPN]] |access-date=July 16, 2021 |date=March 12, 2021}} As a freshman, he averaged 20.1 points, 6.2 rebounds, 3.5 assists, and 1.6 steals per game.{{cite web |last=Rafferty |first=Scott |title=Potential No. 1 pick Cade Cunningham declares for 2021 NBA Draft |url=https://ca.nba.com/news/potential-no-1-pick-cade-cunningham-declares-for-2021-nba-draft/97bajtm35to01cl35qo2evuy1 |website=NBA.com |access-date=July 16, 2021 |date=April 1, 2021}} After his freshman season, Cunningham was recognized as a consensus first-team [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]]. He was the first Oklahoma State player to earn the distinction since [[Bob Kurland]] (1944–46).{{cite web |title=Cade Cunningham Collects NABC Award, Named Consensus First Team All-American |url=https://kfor.com/sports/cade-cunningham-collects-nabc-award-named-consensus-first-team-all-american/ |website=[[KFOR-TV]] |access-date=July 16, 2021 |date=March 18, 2021 |archive-date=July 16, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210716231524/https://kfor.com/sports/cade-cunningham-collects-nabc-award-named-consensus-first-team-all-american/ |url-status=dead }} He became the fourth player to win [[Big 12 Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Big 12 Player of the Year]] and [[Big 12]] Freshman of the Year in the same season, joining [[Marcus Smart]], [[Kevin Durant]], and [[Michael Beasley]].{{cite web |last=Medcalf |first=Myron |title=Oklahoma State freshman Cade Cunningham named Big 12 men's hoops player of the year |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/31029144 |website=[[ESPN]] |access-date=July 16, 2021 |date=March 8, 2021}} He was unanimously selected to the first-team [[List of All-Big 12 Conference men's basketball teams|All-Big 12]], the All-Freshman Team, and the All-Newcomer Team.{{cite web |title=Cade Earns Big 12 Player, Freshman of the Year Awards, Likekele HM All-Conference |url=https://okstate.com/news/2021/3/8/mens-basketball-cade-earns-big-12-player-freshman-of-the-year-awards-likekele-hm-all-conference.aspx |website=Oklahoma State University Athletics |access-date=July 16, 2021 |date=March 8, 2021}} Cunningham received major NCAA Division I freshman of the year honors, among them the [[USBWA National Freshman of the Year|Wayman Tisdale Award]], ''[[Sporting News]]'' Freshman of the Year, and [[National Association of Basketball Coaches]] Freshman of the Year.{{cite web |last=Bonner II |first=Frank |title=OSU's Cade Cunningham named Wayman Tisdale National Freshman of the Year |url=https://tulsaworld.com/sports/college/osu/osus-cade-cunningham-named-wayman-tisdale-national-freshman-of-the-year/article_1d27b26e-8c0d-11eb-bff6-3f410f352016.html |website=[[Tulsa World]] |access-date=July 16, 2021 |date=March 23, 2021}}{{cite web |last=DeCourcy |first=Mike |title=Oklahoma State's Cade Cunningham is Sporting News' Freshman of the Year |url=https://www.sportingnews.com/us/ncaa-basketball/news/cade-cunningham-oklahoma-state-freshman-of-the-year/n3lenorpz4ld1eeeawbxd4bdx |website=[[Sporting News]] |access-date=July 16, 2021 |date=March 9, 2021}}{{cite web |last=Bonner II |first=Frank |title=Cade Cunningham earns NABC Freshman of the Year award |url=https://tulsaworld.com/sports/college/osu/cade-cunningham-earns-nabc-freshman-of-the-year-award/article_d9f2515c-93dc-11eb-abd3-5fe9eb99396d.html |website=[[Tulsa World]] |access-date=July 16, 2021 |date=April 2, 2021}} On April 1, 2021, Cunningham announced that he would enter the [[2021 NBA draft]] and forgo his remaining college eligibility. Analysts regarded him as the consensus [[List of first overall NBA draft picks|number one pick]] in the draft.{{cite web |last=Zucker |first=Joseph |title=Cade Cunningham Officially Declares for 2021 NBA Draft; Possible No. 1 Pick |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2933012-cade-cunningham-officially-declares-for-2021-nba-draft-possible-no-1-pick |website=[[Bleacher Report]] |access-date=May 10, 2021 |date=April 1, 2021}} ==Professional career== ===Detroit Pistons (2021–present)=== ====All-Rookie honors (2021–2022)==== Cunningham was drafted with the [[List of first overall NBA draft picks|first overall pick]] of the [[2021 NBA draft]] by the [[Detroit Pistons]].{{cite web|first=Keith|last=Langlois|title='We want Cade!' – wish granted as Pistons grab Cunningham with No. 1 pick|url=https://www.nba.com/pistons/features/we-want-cade-wish-granted-pistons-grab-cunningham-no-1-pick|website=NBA.com|date=July 29, 2021|access-date=July 30, 2021}} He missed part of training camp, all of preseason, and five of Detroit's first six regular-season games due to an ankle injury.{{cite web|last=Buckley|first=Zach|date=April 14, 2022|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2955308-grading-every-2022-nba-teams-rookie-class|title=Grading Every 2022 NBA Team's Rookie Class|website=Bleacher Report|access-date=April 15, 2022}} In his NBA debut on October 30, Cunningham had two points, two assists, and seven rebounds in 18 minutes in a 110–103 win over the [[Orlando Magic]]. His two points were the fewest scored in a No. 1 pick's NBA debut since [[Anthony Bennett (basketball)|Anthony Bennett]] in 2013, who also had two points.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/32512404 |title=Cade Cunningham to 'play free' after getting past injury-delayed Detroit Pistons debut|last=Woodyard|first=Eric|website=ESPN.com|date=October 30, 2021|access-date=October 30, 2021}} After five games, Cunningham posted his first 40-plus field-goal percentage, and he had an 18-point, 10-rebound [[double-double]] in his third NBA game. On November 15, Cunningham became the youngest player in NBA history to tally at least 25 points, eight rebounds, and eight assists with five three-pointers in a game at 20 years, 51 days. He topped [[LeBron James]] (20 years, 100 days) and [[Trae Young]] (20 years, 163 days).{{cite web|date=November 16, 2021|title=Cade Cunningham becomes youngest ever to record latest stat line|url=https://therookiewire.usatoday.com/2021/11/15/pistons-cade-cunningham-lebron-james/|access-date=December 21, 2021|website=The Rookie Wire}} On November 21, he notched a [[triple-double]] with 13 points, 12 rebounds, and 10 assists in a 121–116 loss to the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] to become the eighth-youngest player in NBA history to record a triple-double and the youngest in Pistons history.{{cite web|date=November 22, 2021|title=Cade Cunningham became youngest Pistons player to notch triple-double|url=https://therookiewire.usatoday.com/2021/11/22/pistons-cade-cunningham-triple-double/|access-date=December 21, 2021|website=The Rookie Wire}} [[File:Cade Cunningham (51914218632).jpg|right|thumb|Cunningham at the [[2022 NBA All-Star Game#Skills Challenge|2022 NBA Skills Challenge]]]] On January 25, 2022, Cunningham recorded 34 points, eight rebounds, eight assists, four blocks, and two steals in a 110–105 loss to the [[Denver Nuggets]], joining [[Michael Jordan]] as the only rookies in NBA history to post such a stat line.{{cite web|first=Omari|last=Sankofa II|title=Cade Cunningham's career night not enough as Detroit Pistons lose to Nuggets, 110-105|url=https://www.freep.com/story/sports/nba/pistons/2022/01/25/cade-cunningham-detroit-pistons-game-recap-denver-nuggets/9218729002/|website=Detroit Free Press|date=January 25, 2022|access-date=February 19, 2022}}{{cite web|first=Lauren|last=Williams|title=Pistons Cade Cunningham joins Michael Jordan in NBA history books following career night|url=https://www.mlive.com/pistons/2022/01/pistons-cade-cunningham-joins-michael-jordan-in-nba-history-books-following-career-night.html|website=MLive|date=January 26, 2022|access-date=February 19, 2022}} He was named the NBA Eastern Conference Rookie of the Month for games played in January.{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/news/nba-rookies-month-january-cade-cunningham-josh-giddey|title=Cade Cunningham, Josh Giddey named NBA Rookies of the Month|website=NBA.com|date=February 2, 2022|access-date=February 4, 2022}} Cunningham was named MVP of the [[Rising Stars Challenge]] on February 18, 2022.{{cite web|first=Tim|last=Bontemps|title=Cade Cunningham named MVP in revamped
